comparison: Perfect agreement on structural modeling claims (C40-C48). Both evaluations find the combination of AlphaFold2 predictions and IP-CLMS validation compelling, with ~85% crosslink compatibility providing strong structural evidence. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Complete agreement on KKT7/KKT9 and KKT8 complex findings (C49-C52, C71). Both evaluations find the RNAi screen and LacI-LacO tethering experiments convincing evidence for CPC recruitment mechanisms. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Full agreement on KKT8 complex structural and biochemical characterization (C53-C57). Both evaluations praise the combination of structural predictions, E. coli reconstitution, IP-CLMS data, and interdependency experiments. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on evolutionary/bioinformatic analysis (C29-C32). Both find the reciprocal BLAST searches and evolutionary context appropriate, though peer review suggests it could be strengthened with additional predictions. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Disagreement on evolutionary speculation (C73). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the claim requires additional phylogenetic analysis and functional studies in other eukaryotes. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, with no direct challenge to the speculation and emphasis on evolutionary significance as a strength.

Disagreement on KIN-A motor activity claims (C4, C62-C69). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the rigor mutant experiments provide strong evidence. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting that while data are 'highly suggestive,' definitive biochemical evidence of ATPase activity is lacking.

Agreement on CD1/CD2 domain findings (C58-C61), though peer R6 also includes C3. Both evaluations find the AlphaFold2 predictions combined with domain deletion experiments convincing. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on KIN-A/KIN-B as CPC components (C1, C24-C28). Both evaluations find IP-MS and colocalization data compelling. OpenEval R1 includes additional claims (C2, C70, C72, C25, C26, C27, C28) while peer R1 focuses on core identification. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on hierarchical dependencies within CPC (C34-C39). OpenEval R2 includes C33 while peer R2 includes C2 and C72. Both find RNAi depletion experiments and domain deletions rigorous and convincing. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Overlap on C33 (RNAi depletion causing growth defects). OpenEval R2 includes this as part of broader hierarchical dependency analysis (SUPPORTED). Peer R9 treats it as confirmatory of previous work rather than novel, but still SUPPORTED.

Overlap on C70 (novel CPC localization pathways). OpenEval R1 includes C70 as part of broader evidence for KIN-A/KIN-B as CPC components. Peer R10 treats this as the central conclusion of the paper. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Overlap on C2 and C72 (hierarchical organization and localization regulation). OpenEval R1 groups these with KIN-A/KIN-B identification claims. Peer R2 focuses on epistasis analysis and RNAi experiments. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on C6 (central spindle localization). OpenEval R7 includes C6 as part of motor activity analysis. Peer R11 addresses C5 and C6 as integrative conclusion about 'two-in-one' localization modules. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R9 addresses background/literature claims (C7-C23) as appropriately cited established knowledge (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are contextual rather than novel findings.
